_comment: The DEFAULT PR risk map for the reusable pr-risk.yml workflow. VERSIONED so a later
revision can be REPLAYED against accumulated graded records rather than reconstructed —
every graded record carries the map_version that produced it.
This default is deliberately GENERIC: it names ecosystem-level risk classes (CI, deps,
migrations, IaC, secrets, API contracts), never any one repo's internal layout. A consumer
repo sharpens it by committing .github/risk.json; the workflow reads that file from the
PR's BASE ref, so a PR cannot edit the rules that judge it — the same defence pr-size.yml
TIERS: R0 safest .. R3 riskiest. grade = worst(path_floor, provenance, reversibility):
each axis independently PROPOSES a tier and the worst wins, so no axis can ever move a PR
into a SAFER lane than another axis put it.
GLOBS: `**` crosses directory separators, `*` does not. Matching is whole-path anchored.

path_rules.why: touching the map itself is automatically R3 — a PR must not be able to lower its own grade
CODEOWNERS decides who must review — editing it edits the review gate
any workflow file is automatically R3 — a workflow runs with repo credentials
schema migrations mutate persistent state and do not cleanly revert
infrastructure as code — blast radius is the estate, not the request
dependency manifests pull in code nobody in the PR wrote — every ecosystem, not just one (a package.json `scripts` block is supply-chain-relevant in exactly the same way go.mod is)
cross-repo API contract — consumers break out of band
data deletion / compliance — irreversible by construction
test-only changes cannot break production behaviour

_path_rule_order: R3 classes are listed FIRST but ORDER DOES NOT MATTER: the path floor is the WORST tier over every rule any changed path matches, so an R0 doc rule can never cancel an R3 migration rule in the same PR.

provenance_tiers._why: external (a fork / first-time contributor) is R3 on provenance alone — an unreviewed outside diff is the one provenance class never routed unattended. runbook is R0 ONLY when the shape assertion also holds (see the runbook registry); a claimed-but-shape-failed runbook falls back to its underlying class.

reversibility._why_irreversible: a PR touching these mutates persistent state or deletes data — reverting the code does not restore the state, so reversibility is pinned R3 regardless of how clean the diff is.
reversibility._why_delete: a DELETED file under a persistent-state or trust-boundary class is not a clean single revert — R3.
reversibility._why_no_green: did tests covering the touched lines actually run? A PR with no GREEN check rollup cannot answer yes, so it cannot be graded safer than R2.
reversibility._why_no_test: green checks but the diff touches no test file: the suite ran, but nothing proves it covers THESE lines.

_flippable: a change gated behind a flippable flag is recoverable without a deploy. Recorded on the reversibility axis as `flag_gated`; in v0 it is REPORTED, never used to LOWER a tier (an axis may only move a PR riskier).
